"""Reads the molecules and computes their properties with RDKit. A SMILES that
cannot be read is reported with the reason and skipped."""
import tsugumi
import numpy as np
from rdkit import Chem, RDLogger
from rdkit.Chem import Crippen, Descriptors, Lipinski, rdMolDescriptors

from inputs.pasted.mol.Pasted import Pasted
from tsugumi import Failure

RDLogger.DisableLog("rdApp.*")  # reasons are shown on the Card instead


def read(smiles):
    """The molecule and None, or None and why it could not be read."""
    mol = Chem.MolFromSmiles(smiles, sanitize=False)
    if mol is None:
        return None, "it cannot be parsed as SMILES"
    problems = Chem.DetectChemistryProblems(mol)
    if problems:
        return None, f"it does not make chemical sense (RDKit: {problems[0].Message()})"
    Chem.SanitizeMol(mol)
    return mol, None


def entries(inputs):
    """(name, SMILES) from the list, then the pasted one."""
    p = inputs.params
    pairs = []
    for i in range(len(p.molecules)):
        name, _, smiles = p.molecules[i].decode().partition(":")
        pairs.append((name.strip(), smiles.strip()) if smiles else (f"#{i + 1}", name.strip()))
    pasted = inputs.input("pasted", Pasted)
    smiles = (pasted.Smiles() or b"").decode().strip()
    if smiles:
        pairs.append(((pasted.Name() or b"pasted").decode().strip() or "pasted", smiles))
    return pairs


def strings(items):
    offsets = [s for s in items]
    _b_items = []
    for o in reversed(offsets):
        _b_items.append(o)
    return list(reversed(_b_items))


def main(inputs, report):
    rows, errors = [], []
    for name, smiles in entries(inputs):
        mol, why = read(smiles)
        if mol is None:
            errors.append(f"The SMILES `{smiles}` of **{name}** was left out of the computation: {why}.")
            report.log(str(f"skipped {name}: {smiles}: {why}"))
            continue
        rows.append(dict(
            name=name, smiles=smiles, formula=rdMolDescriptors.CalcMolFormula(mol),
            mw=Descriptors.MolWt(mol), logp=Crippen.MolLogP(mol), tpsa=rdMolDescriptors.CalcTPSA(mol),
            hbd=rdMolDescriptors.CalcNumHBD(mol), hba=rdMolDescriptors.CalcNumHBA(mol),
            rotatable=rdMolDescriptors.CalcNumRotatableBonds(mol),
            nh_oh=Lipinski.NHOHCount(mol), n_o=Lipinski.NOCount(mol),
        ))
    if not rows:
        raise Failure("output_invalid", "no readable molecule: " + " ".join(errors))

    lines = [*errors, ""] if errors else []
    lines += [f"**Properties of {len(rows)} molecules** (computed with RDKit)", "",
              "| Name | Formula | Molecular weight | logP | TPSA (Å²) | HBD | HBA | Rotatable bonds |",
              "| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |"]
    lines += [f"| {r['name']} | {r['formula']} | {r['mw']:.2f} | {r['logp']:.2f} | {r['tpsa']:.2f} | "
              f"{r['hbd']} | {r['hba']} | {r['rotatable']} |" for r in rows]
    report.markdown("\n".join(lines))
    (names, smiles, formula) = (strings([r[k] for r in rows]) for k in ('name', 'smiles', 'formula'))
    doubles = [np.array([r[k] for r in rows], dtype=np.float64) for k in ('mw', 'logp', 'tpsa')]
    ints = [np.array([r[k] for r in rows], dtype=np.int32) for k in ('hbd', 'hba', 'rotatable', 'nh_oh', 'n_o')]
    _out_value = {}
    _out_value['names'] = names
    _out_value['smiles'] = smiles
    _out_value['formula'] = formula
    _out_value['mw'] = doubles[0]
    _out_value['logp'] = doubles[1]
    _out_value['tpsa'] = doubles[2]
    _out_value['hbd'] = ints[0]
    _out_value['hba'] = ints[1]
    _out_value['rotatable'] = ints[2]
    _out_value['nh_oh'] = ints[3]
    _out_value['n_o'] = ints[4]
    return {'molecules': _out_value}

"""The structures as a grid, drawn by RDKit, labelled by matplotlib (which has Japanese glyphs)."""
import math

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from rdkit import Chem
from rdkit.Chem import Draw

from inputs.molecules.mol.Molecules import Molecules


def main(inputs, report):
    m = inputs.input("molecules", Molecules)
    n = m.NamesLength()
    cols = min(5, n)
    rows = math.ceil(n / cols)
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(rows, cols, figsize=(2.7 * cols, 2.6 * rows), squeeze=False)
    for ax in axes.ravel():
        ax.axis("off")
    for i in range(n):
        ax = axes.ravel()[i]
        ax.imshow(Draw.MolToImage(Chem.MolFromSmiles(m.Smiles(i).decode()), size=(420, 360)))
        ax.set_title(f"{m.Names(i).decode()}\n{m.Formula(i).decode()}", fontsize=10)
    fig.tight_layout()
    report.figure()

"""Lipinski's rule of five, with his counts: NH + OH for donors, N + O for acceptors."""
import tsugumi
import numpy as np

from inputs.molecules.mol.Molecules import Molecules

RULES = [("molecular weight > 500", "mw", 500), ("logP > 5", "logp", 5), ("NH+OH > 5", "nh_oh", 5), ("N+O > 10", "n_o", 10)]


def strings(items):
    offsets = [s for s in items]
    _b_items = []
    for o in reversed(offsets):
        _b_items.append(o)
    return list(reversed(_b_items))


def cell(value, limit, digits=0):
    text = f"{value:.{digits}f}"
    return f"**{text}**" if value > limit else text


def main(inputs, report):
    m = inputs.input("molecules", Molecules)
    limit = inputs.params.maxViolations
    n = m.NamesLength()
    names = [m.Names(i).decode() for i in range(n)]
    formula = [m.Formula(i).decode() for i in range(n)]
    values = dict(mw=m.MwAsNumpy(), logp=m.LogpAsNumpy(), nh_oh=m.NhOhAsNumpy(), n_o=m.NOAsNumpy())
    broken = [[label for label, key, top in RULES if values[key][i] > top] for i in range(n)]
    violations = np.array([len(b) for b in broken], dtype=np.int32)
    passed = violations <= limit
    report.log(str(f"{int(passed.sum())} of {n} pass with at most {limit} violations; violations "
          + ", ".join(f"{names[i]} {violations[i]}" for i in range(n))))

    lines = [f"**{int(passed.sum())} of {n} molecules pass** (up to {limit} violations; values over the limit in bold)", "",
             "| Name | Molecular weight | logP | NH+OH | N+O | Violations | Verdict |", "| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |"]
    for i in range(n):
        lines.append(f"| {names[i]} | {cell(values['mw'][i], 500, 1)} | {cell(values['logp'][i], 5, 2)} | "
                     f"{cell(values['nh_oh'][i], 5)} | {cell(values['n_o'][i], 10)} | {violations[i]} | "
                     f"{'pass' if passed[i] else '**fail**'} |")
    report.markdown("\n".join(lines))
    names_v = strings(names)
    formula_v = strings(formula)
    broken_v = strings([', '.join(x) for x in broken])
    doubles = [v for v in (m.MwAsNumpy(), m.LogpAsNumpy(), m.TpsaAsNumpy())]
    violations_v = violations
    _out_value = {}
    _out_value['names'] = names_v
    _out_value['formula'] = formula_v
    _out_value['mw'] = doubles[0]
    _out_value['logp'] = doubles[1]
    _out_value['tpsa'] = doubles[2]
    _out_value['violations'] = violations_v
    _out_value['broken'] = broken_v
    _out_value['max_violations'] = limit
    return {'checked': _out_value}

"""Tanimoto similarity of Morgan fingerprints for every pair of molecules."""
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
from rdkit import Chem, DataStructs
from rdkit.Chem import rdFingerprintGenerator

from inputs.molecules.mol.Molecules import Molecules


def main(inputs, report):
    m = inputs.input("molecules", Molecules)
    p = inputs.params
    n = m.NamesLength()
    names = [m.Names(i).decode() for i in range(n)]
    generator = rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganGenerator(radius=p.radius, fpSize=p.bits)
    prints = [generator.GetFingerprint(Chem.MolFromSmiles(m.Smiles(i).decode())) for i in range(n)]
    sim = np.array([DataStructs.BulkTanimotoSimilarity(f, prints) for f in prints])
    off = sim - np.eye(n)
    a, b = np.unravel_index(np.argmax(off), off.shape)
    mean = off.sum() / max(n * (n - 1), 1)
    report.log(str(f"mean similarity {mean:.4f}; most similar {names[a]} and {names[b]} {sim[a, b]:.4f}"))

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 6.6))
    image = ax.imshow(sim, cmap="Blues", vmin=0, vmax=1)
    ax.set_xticks(range(n), names, rotation=45, ha="right")
    ax.set_yticks(range(n), names)
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(n):
            ax.text(j, i, f"{sim[i, j]:.2f}"[1:] if sim[i, j] < 1 else "1", ha="center", va="center", fontsize=8,
                    color="white" if sim[i, j] > 0.55 else "#333333")
    ax.set_title(f"Tanimoto coefficient (Morgan radius {p.radius}): the closest are {names[a]} and {names[b]} ({sim[a, b]:.2f})",
                 fontsize=11)
    fig.colorbar(image, ax=ax, shrink=0.8)
    fig.tight_layout()
    report.figure()

notes.html:
Molecular properties and the Rule of Five

From SMILES, which writes a molecule as a string, RDKit computes properties. The molecular weight is the sum of the atomic weights.

M=∑ini AiM = \sum_i n_i\, A_i

Lipinski's Rule of Five is a rule of thumb for molecules readily absorbed when taken orally: violating two or more of the following is said to make absorption poor.

M≤500,log⁡P≤5,NH+OH≤5,N+O≤10M \le 500,\quad \log P \le 5,\quad \mathrm{NH{+}OH} \le 5,\quad \mathrm{N{+}O} \le 10

Paste a SMILES into smiles of paste and run, and that molecule joins every Card. A SMILES that cannot be read shows the reason instead of crashing.

logP is an estimate by summing atomic contributions (Crippen), not a measurement. A rule of thumb has exceptions, and it does not decide whether a drug is good.
